title: An intercepted `navigation.navigate()` cancels an ongoing cross-document navigation, which breaks links while React's transition indicator runs [zcorpan/navigation-api-qa]

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
In *[navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate)*, step 20 sets the ongoing navigation before step 22 fires the `navigate` event:

> Set the ongoing navigation for *navigable* to *navigationId*.
>
> Note: This will have the effect of aborting other ongoing navigations of *navigable*, ...

So a `navigation.navigate()` that a `navigate` handler then intercepts still cancels a cross-document navigation already in flight. [intercept-stops-ongoing-cross-document-navigation.html](https://wpt.fyi/results/navigation-api/navigate-event/intercept-stops-ongoing-cross-document-navigation.html) expects this; it passes in Safari TP and fails in Chrome Canary and Firefox Nightly.

React DOM 19's default transition indicator relies on the other behavior. While a transition is pending, it calls `navigation.navigate(currentEntry.url, {history: "replace", info: "react-transition"})` and intercepts it with a promise that settles when the transition ends. When that navigation fails, for example because the user clicked a link, it restarts it 20 ms later ([ReactDOMDefaultTransitionIndicator.js](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/76baa3b5434fad315ece9cfd4d20d7a8d6c34a25/packages/react-dom/src/client/ReactDOMDefaultTransitionIndicator.js#L42-L75)). If the link is cross-document and its response takes longer than that, the restart cancels the user's navigation.

[Test case](https://github.com/zcorpan/navigation-api-qa/blob/6394f99fb120977f139a718c15960d3672e19ac1/findings/03-spec-intercepted-navigate-cancels-cross-document/test.html) (served by the repo's `server.py`, for the slow response): the indicator code from React's production bundle, then a click on a same-origin link whose response takes 150 ms. In Safari TP the click does nothing and the page stays; the same happens with a script click and with `location.href`. Chrome Canary and Firefox Nightly leave the page. With a fast response, each of them leaves the page.

The indicator code is in 2,866 desktop or mobile pages of HTTP Archive's top-10k sample. It only runs during a React transition, so I don't know how often users hit this. #12820 and #11745 are related: React skips the restart when `navigation.transition` is non-null, but that's only set for intercepted navigations.

(Found in https://github.com/zcorpan/navigation-api-qa.)
